memory.content: The user wants Chief of Staff as the main point of contact: they send tasks here, and this agent delegates work to other bots rather than doing everything itself.
Prefer specialists per communications channel rather than one mega-comms agent, with Chief of Staff as the front door and no extra comms-manager layer unless the specialist list gets noisy.
Do not accept mailbox passwords in chat.
Promo and marketing email should be archived rather than deleted, keeping only messages that look actually for the user.
Marketing sequence for launches: organic and owned audience first, then pitching, paid last. Music or Release Ops owns distribution; LinkedIn stays professional networking.
When a debut release starts a whole project brand, use project-launch strategies (identity, origin story, first-touch capture), not follow-up single promo tactics.

Prefer referring to specialist agents by individual name; use specialists or the team for the group; Agent is the accurate product term and Bot is fine informally; reserve assistant for the Chief of Staff front-door role.

A Usage specialist monitors Grok Bot included and on-demand usage. Default: observe and alert only — do not stop other agents' needed work; only recommend slowdown or postpone unless the user approves a throttle.
For usage, prefer a short chat one-liner (percent used + days left) over screenshots; check midweek and before weekly reset, not frequently.

For creative brand social bios, keep copy project-first and name-free when the brand is the public face. Never use em dashes in any public or posted copy; use an ellipsis (…) or a semicolon (;) to separate ideas.
A custom project tracker MCP (assets, plans, actions, site health) may be connected separately from marketplace plugins; connect it with the user's own endpoint and auth — no secrets in memory.
When Spark or another desktop mail client has no connector, use Gmail as the integration path and server-side forward leftover mailboxes into the connected Gmail when possible.

skills.name: Specialist swarm Chief of Staff
skills.description: Use this when setting up or running a front-door Chief of Staff that delegates to named specialist agents instead of doing every channel itself.
skills.content:
---
name: Specialist swarm Chief of Staff
description: >-
  Use this when setting up or running a front-door Chief of Staff that delegates
  to named specialist agents instead of doing every channel itself.
---
# Specialist swarm Chief of Staff

## Goal
Make one front-door assistant the user’s only intake, then route work to named specialists so channels stay focused and the user is not buried in parallel chats.

## Default roster (create only what the user needs)
- **Email** — inbox triage, drafts, archive/trash rules
- **Calendar** — scheduling, briefs, reminders
- **Messages** — Slack/SMS/chat once connected
- **Projects** — project tracker / source of truth for assets and plans
- **Music** (or Release Ops) — production, distribution, publishing for creative releases
- **Marketing** — campaign strategy and calendars
- **Social** — short-form and profile presence
- **Audience** — owned list / CRM / welcome sequences
- **Reach** — pitching and paid (last)
- **Art** / **Photos** / **Figma** — visuals vs photo library vs design files
- **Usage** — usage alerts only; never silently stop needed work
- Channel specialists as needed: GitHub, LinkedIn, etc.

## Operating rules
1. User talks to Chief of Staff only. CoS delegates with a clear ask, success criteria, and what to report back.
2. Prefer specialists per channel over one mega-comms agent. Add a manager layer only if the roster gets noisy.
3. Call specialists by name. Reserve “assistant” for the front door; “agent” / “bot” for the team.
4. No posts, uploads, sends, pitches, or spend without explicit user OK.
5. Fan-out only when the user asks or clearly needs parallel specialists; otherwise propose first.
6. Keep private credentials out of chat. Never accept mailbox passwords in chat.
7. Usage agent observes and recommends throttles; it does not unilaterally stop other agents’ needed work.

## First-run setup
1. Confirm the user wants CoS as the only front door.
2. Create the smallest roster for their current goals (often Email + Calendar + Projects first).
3. Connect marketplace connectors the roster needs (Gmail, Calendar, GitHub, etc.).
4. Write short profile memories: routing map, confirmation gates, archive vs trash preferences.
5. Add routines for recurring checks (domain expiry, usage midweek/pre-reset, morning calendar brief on the Calendar agent).

## Handback
When a specialist finishes, CoS summarizes outcomes for the user in one place and queues the next gate that needs a human OK.

skills.name: Creative project launch ops
skills.description: Use this when launching a creative brand or debut single with specialists for release, marketing, social, audience, and visuals — profiles and drafts first, nothing live without OK.
skills.content:
---
name: Creative project launch ops
description: >-
  Use this when launching a creative brand or debut single with specialists for
  release, marketing, social, audience, and visuals — profiles and drafts first,
  nothing live without OK.
---
# Creative project launch ops

## Goal
Launch a creative project (artist, album, or debut single that starts a brand) with a specialist swarm: organic and owned audience first, then pitching, paid last. Profiles and drafts can proceed; posts, uploads, sends, pitches, and spend wait for explicit OK.

## Sequence
1. **Lock the story** — project identity, origin story, debut asset, distributor path.
2. **Stand specialists** — Music/Release, Marketing, Social, Audience, Reach, Art/Photos/Figma, Projects as source of truth.
3. **Profiles before posts** — claim accounts; bios are project-first and name-free when the brand is the public face. Treat niche platforms as a depth layer beside mainstream short-form.
4. **Assets** — cover/art lock, mix/master path, metadata checklist (ISRC, UPC, date, credits).
5. **Owned audience** — capture landing + welcome sequence drafts; no live sends until OK.
6. **Soft-tease calendar** — draft only until Music assets are ready and the user greenlights content.
7. **Reach** — pitch list and EPK outline after organic/owned foundation; paid last.

## Public copy rules
- Prefer project-first, name-free bios on social when the brand (not the person) is the face.
- Never use em dashes in public or posted copy; use an ellipsis (…) or a semicolon (;) to separate ideas.
- Website About may stay personally signed if the user wants that.

## Confirmation gates
Hold until the user OK’s: live posts, uploads, distributor submit, email sends, pitches, and any paid spend.

## Marketing posture for a debut that starts a brand
Use project-launch tactics (identity, origin story, first-touch capture), not “next single” promo tactics.

routines.name: Domain expiry reminder
routines.description: Weekday check that nudges before a watched domain renews so it does not lapse unnoticed.
routines.content:
Remind the user that their watched domain is approaching expiry (registrar fill-in). Keep the related expiry notice in mail; do not let Email trash it.

Stay quiet unless a reminder is due. Use today's date in the user's local timezone:

- If more than 14 days before expiry: only remind on Mondays.
- If 8–14 days before expiry: remind Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.
- If 7 days or fewer before expiry, on expiry day, or after expiry with no confirmation it was renewed: remind every weekday this fires.

Keep it short: domain, date, registrar, days left (or that it has expired). After the user confirms it is renewed, delete this routine.

Fill-ins:
- {{domain}} — domain name to watch
- {{expiry_date}} — expiry date
- {{registrar}} — registrar name (e.g. GoDaddy)

Fires on:
- cron `27 9 * * 1-5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
